problem: Customers rated the product poorly compared with rivals.
title: Domino's rebuilds its pizza recipe and admits the old one was weak
context: Domino's core pizza was criticised by customers and the company's domestic sales were roughly flat in 2009.
decision_made: Reformulate the core pizza and openly acknowledge past flaws in advertising.
action_taken: Launched the new recipe in late December 2009 with ads showing customer criticism and employee responses.
observed_outcome: Domestic same-store sales rose 14.3 percent in Q1 2010. The CEO credited the new pizza and the candour of the marketing; some analysts credited the advertising or curiosity more than the recipe.
lessons: Admitting a product weakness while fixing it can win back attention, but the cause of the sales jump is hard to separate.
limitations: Short observation window, curiosity effects, and mixed analyst views on cause. Company statements are self-reported.

claims.claim_text: Domino's reformulated its core pizza and ran ads that acknowledged the old product's flaws.
Domestic same-store sales rose 14.3 percent in the first quarter of 2010.
